## Natural history notes

A medium-sized bumble bee characterized by its fuzzy black-and-yellow body, pale yellow thorax, and two yellow spots or patches on the front of the abdomen that help give the species its name. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, roadsides, and other open or semi-open habitats with abundant flowering plants, especially in the northern part of the state. Adults visit many flowers for nectar and pollen and are important pollinators, while colonies nest in abandoned rodent burrows, grass tussocks, or other sheltered cavities near the ground.
